La recta era la figura de una ecuación d: The line was the figure of a first-degree equation. The conics are the figures of second-degree equations in $x$ and $y$, and they are all defined with Pythagoras' tool: the distance between two points. A circle is “points at distance $r$ from the centre”; the others swap that condition for another about distances to one or two fixed points.
Coge un cono y córtalo con un plano. Seg: Take a cone and cut it with a plane. According to the tilt of the cut, four different curves come out: circle, ellipse, parabola and hyperbola. That is why they are called conics. That these four very different curves are the same thing seen another way is one of the loveliest discoveries of Greek geometry.

Apolonio de Perga escribió las <em>Cónic: Apollonius of Perga wrote the Conics around 200 BC: eight books, and he gave them the names we still use. For 1800 years they were pure mathematics with no known application. Until in 1609 Kepler discovered that the planets describe ellipses, and Galileo that projectiles follow parabolas. It is mathematicians' favourite example for defending research with no immediate application.

As it turns, the stick draws a perfect ellipse, because the length of the string — the sum of the two distances — does not change.

Las cónicas son las trayectorias del uni: The conics are the paths of the universe. Kepler discovered that the planets describe ellipses with the Sun at one focus, and since then all celestial mechanics is the geometry of conics: a satellite in orbit goes in an ellipse, a probe escaping the solar system goes in a hyperbola, and a thrown stone describes a piece of a parabola. The focus property of the parabola is what makes a satellite dish concentrate the whole signal at one point, and the ellipse's explains whispering galleries, where a murmur at one focus is heard clearly at the other.

La excentricidad de la órbita terrestre: The eccentricity of the Earth's orbit is 0.017: almost zero, that is, almost a circle. That tiny figure has enormous consequences, because its variations over tens of thousands of years are one of the causes of the ice ages. In comets, by contrast, the eccentricity is around 0.97, and that is why they pass close to the Sun once and disappear for decades.
La primera matemática de la que se conse: The first woman mathematician of whom reliable record survives is Hypatia of Alexandria, who lived between the fourth and fifth centuries. She ran a school of philosophy in Alexandria, taught astronomy and mathematics, and according to ancient sources wrote commentaries on works of Diophantus and Ptolemy and prepared an edition of Apollonius' Conics, the book this whole topic comes from. She was murdered in 415 by a mob, amid the religious and political strife of the city, and in time she became a symbol of learning persecuted.
